title: A borosilicate glass plate quenched from 90 C into 20 C water: thermal shock, the surface in tension (demonstration)

provenance.purpose: the library's elasticity driven by a field in time (G24): the plate's temperature written as a field with water exchanging heat at its faces, the solid strained by it at every output time. An eighth of a plate 40 x 40 x 4 mm by symmetry. A demonstration: the water's heat transfer coefficient is assumed, and Manson's estimate for an infinite plate is the textbook comparison, not a measurement (on 2026-10-09 the face's centre peaked at 7.13 MPa, 3.1 % under Manson's 7.37 MPa, and the plate's edge, cooled from two sides, at 9.02 MPa)
provenance.material: SCHOTT BOROFLOAT 33: density 2.23 g/cm3, E 64 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.2, cp 0.83 kJ/(kg K) at 20 to 100 C, conductivity 1.2 W/(m K) at 90 C (schott.com, BOROFLOAT 33 technical details); expansion 3.25e-6 /K, 20 to 300 C (SCHOTT BOROFLOAT 33 technical data sheet, ISO 7991)
provenance.assumed: the water's heat transfer coefficient, 2000 W/(m^2 K), still water without boiling (the glass starts below 100 C)

borofloat 33.source: SCHOTT BOROFLOAT 33: schott.com technical details (density, E, Poisson's ratio, cp at 20 to 100 C, conductivity at 90 C) and its technical data sheet (expansion 20 to 300 C, ISO 7991)
